div.head: V Atr 32
div.ab: ⁊ æfre alicgan heonan forð þa unlaga, þe ær þysan wæran to gewunelice wide.
⁊ æfre alicgan heonan forð þa unlaga, þe ær þysan [wæran] to gewunelice wide.
⁊ æfre alecgan heonan forð þa unlaga þe ure hlaford oft ⁊ gelome silf het alecgan.
And æfre alicgan heonan forð þa unlaga þe ær þysan wæran to gewunelice wide.
And there shall henceforth be an end to the unjust practices which our lord himself has frequently and often commanded us to stop.
And forever henceforth the unlawful practices are to cease which beforehand were too often found widely:
And ever henceforth the abuses are to cease which hitherto have been too common far and wide.

Und stets hinfort sollen die Rechtsmissbräuche unterbleiben, die vordem allzu gewöhnlich verbreitet gewesen sind (sollen sie die R. ablegen, die unser Herr selbst oft und häufig abzuschaffen befahl D).
And let the abuses which were all too common before now always cease henceforth (let them lay aside the abuses which our lord himself has often and frequently ordered abolished, D).
div.note: In G2, ‘wæran’ was written above the line later.
VI Ethelred omits this chapter, but adds (39): “And if any one defiles a nun or ravishes a widow, he is to atone for it deeply both to the Church and the state”.

The Corpus MS. words this clause differently, and adds some instances of the abuses in question. It runs: 32. And ever henceforth are the abuses to cease which our lord himself has again and again ordered to be suppressed. 32.1. First, namely, concerning the attaching of property, which deceiving rogues have readily practised in the West, who have harassed and wrongfully afflicted many a man.
ær . . . wide: ure hlaford oft and gelome silf het alecgan D 32.1–5 These clauses are found only in D.
